title: Introduce econ-orchestrator governor and safe compact profile rollforward
author: Lina Becker
description:
Motivation: production workloads report oscillating batch sizes and noisy quantization rollouts across heterogeneous fleets. This PR introduces a runtime-side 'Econ Orchestrator Governor' that applies hysteresis and safe rollforward semantics to batching and compact/quantization profile changes to reduce unit-cost churn while preserving latency SLOs.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a governor process that: (a) observes recent per-route latency/cost statistics, (b) computes stable batching targets using hysteresis windows to avoid flip-flops, (c) stages compact/quant profile rollforwards with canary windows and metric guards, and (d) exposes opt-in defaults for workspace-level econ profiles.

Key changes: 
- runtime/orchestrator: new governor implementation (governor.py) with hysteresis and stable-state detection; eventing hooks for policy engine.
- configs/econ_profiles/compact_defaults.yaml: curated conservative compact/quant profile defaults tuned for balanced latency/cost for small/med/large models.
- rollout logic: safe rollforward path that performs metric-based canaries (latency/accuracy/99p token-time) and automatic rollback on regressions.
- migration: workspace migration that annotates existing profiles with an opt-in 'governor:enabled' flag; default remains off for Dedicated customers unless explicitly enabled.
- console: UI panels to visualize governor decisions and canary progress (docs only; UI surfaces behind feature flag).
- tests: unit + integration tests that simulate oscillating load and quant rollforward scenarios.

Checklist:
- [x] Core governor implementation and unit tests
- [x] Canary and rollback plumbing with metric thresholds
- [x] Conservative default profiles for compact quantization
- [x] Integration tests covering hysteresis behavior
- [x] Documentation and RFC (docs/rfcs/econ-governor.md)
- [x] Backwards-compatible migration path

Risks and mitigations: the governor influences runtime decisions; it is gated by workspace opt-in and feature flagging. Rollforward always starts with a small canary fraction and metric guards to auto-rollback on P95/P99 or accuracy regressions. We also added observable traces and alerts for unexpected oscillations.

Related work: builds on ENG-7721 (batching heuristics) and ENG-8245 (quant profile metadata). Linear tickets: ENG-8742 (governor design), ENG-8899 (experimentation harness). Jira SUP-1187 captures customer request for safer quant rollouts.

release_notes: Added Econ Orchestrator Governor to provide stable batching targets and safe compact/quant profile rollforwards. Opt-in by workspace; conservative defaults provided. See RFC docs/rfcs/econ-governor.md for configuration guide and migration steps.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated. To enable for a workspace: set workspace.config.gov_enabled=true and pick a compact profile in configs/econ_profiles/compact_defaults.yaml. Watch gov.decision_rate and gov.rollback_alert metrics. Canary defaults to 1% traffic and will auto-rollback on P99 or accuracy regressions.
testing_instructions: Run unit tests: pytest tests/unit/test_governor_state_machine.py. Integration: pytest tests/integration/test_governor_hysteresis.py --runslow. To simulate rollforward: use scripts/simulate_rollforward.py --profile small-conservative --traffic-pattern burst --observe-metrics.
